taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems erect, slender, mostly 3-15 dm (1-25 dm at the extremes).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stems to 25 dm at most.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves 4-10 cm (2-17 cm at the extremes).

traits.leaflets.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets 5-9 (to 11); 7-9 in var. gymnocarpa.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa var. gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves 3-6 cm wide (1.5-8 at the extremes).

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet blade 10-40 mm long (4-60 at the extremes).

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): terminal leaflet blade 10-20 mm wide (4-40 at the extremes).

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet blades elliptic to obovate or ovate, membranous.

traits.leaf_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet apex obtuse, sometimes nearly acute.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflet margins doubly serrate, 7-13 gland-tipped teeth a side.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): inflorescences corymbs, usually of 1-3 flowers.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): corymbs usually 1-3-flowered.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): pedicels slender, 15-25 mm (10-35).

traits.flower_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowers 1.5-3 cm across.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals 8-15 mm long.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals lanceolate, 5-10 mm.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals deep pink; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens about 57.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): carpels 3-12 (to 16).

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): hips 7-15 mm long.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): hips 5-13 mm wide.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): hips irregularly ellipsoid to nearly globose.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): hips scarlet; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals, styles and the top of the receptacle fall together from the ripe hip along a clean ring (hence baldhip).

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa var. gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): flowering April to July (from February).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: hips ripe August to October.

traits.stem_clump.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): shrubs, usually loosely clustered: a few slender stems.

traits.spine_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): prickles below the stipules 0-2, erect, slender, 2-8 (to 10) mm.

traits.bark_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): bark reddish brown with age; sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 9 (2014), Rosa gymnocarpa var. gymnocarpa (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaflets usually bright green, dull above; sRGB by eye for the words.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a slender, loosely branched shrub of the forest shade with reddish-brown stems, bright green leaves of small rounded leaflets, and small deep-pink single roses.

allometry.note: 1.3 m tall at 10 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
